findings.highlight: The wind must be surrounding Saber
findings.evidenceJa: 風はセイバーを中心に渦巻いており
findings.governingReading: The wind is swirling around Saber as its center.
findings.explanation: A source assertion becomes a conjecture in the classic branch.

findings.highlight: But I can’t help it because..
findings.evidenceJa: しょうがないじゃないか
findings.governingReading: Shirou cannot help recalling the image whenever the mark throbs.
findings.explanation: The double period and stranded “because” break the sentence at its emotional hinge.

findings.highlight: I lie down
findings.evidenceJa: 身を伏せて
findings.governingReading: Shirou keeps his body low against the wind while putting a foot on the stone steps.
findings.explanation: The English makes him lie down while simultaneously climbing, corrupting the physical staging.

findings.highlight: It must be luck that I avoided it.
findings.evidenceJa: それを避けられたのは偶然か
findings.governingReading: Shirou wonders whether avoiding the dagger-like object was chance.
findings.explanation: An open question becomes a confident explanation.

findings.highlight: if it is only here to watch
findings.evidenceJa: おまえの秘剣を盗み見るだけが目的なのか
findings.governingReading: The hidden observer may be trying to steal a look at Saber’s secret technique.
findings.explanation: The English reduces targeted observation of a secret technique to generic watching.

findings.highlight: this is less interesting now
findings.evidenceJa: あまり気乗りのする話ではない
findings.governingReading: Assassin finds either prospect unappealing and is reluctant to continue under those conditions.
findings.explanation: Reluctance and distaste become a mild loss of entertainment.

findings.highlight: I could have shown you my full secret technique
findings.evidenceJa: 秘剣の全てを味わえた
findings.governingReading: Assassin says he could have savored the whole of Saber’s secret technique.
findings.explanation: The English reverses who would experience whose secret technique.

findings.highlight: we were interrupted at a bad time
findings.evidenceJa: よい所で邪魔が入った
findings.governingReading: The duel was interrupted just as it reached a particularly good or crucial point.
findings.explanation: The English reverses Assassin’s evaluative description of the moment.

findings.highlight: Not because of Assassin’s words, but Saber herself
findings.evidenceJa: アサシンの言葉ではないが、セイバー自身
findings.governingReading: Assassin’s words aside, Saber herself appears to recognize the disadvantage.
findings.explanation: A discursive qualification becomes a denial that his words caused her judgment.

findings.highlight: your pick-up is here as well
findings.evidenceJa: 迎えも来ている
findings.governingReading: Assassin notes that someone has come to fetch or meet Saber.
findings.explanation: “Pick-up” gives the formal warning a casual, object-like register.

findings.highlight: He must have become a spirit
findings.evidenceJa: そうしてアサシンの姿は消えた
findings.governingReading: Assassin disappears from view; the narration does not specify the mechanism.
findings.explanation: The classic branch inserts a speculative spiritualization absent from the active Japanese.

findings.highlight: she quietly stands there
findings.evidenceJa: ぼう、と立ち尽くしている
findings.governingReading: Saber stands motionless in a blank or dazed state.
findings.explanation: The English keeps the posture but removes the marked mental state.

findings.highlight: I’ll bring it up when you wake up
findings.evidenceJa: 目を覚ましたらとっちめてやる
findings.governingReading: Shirou mutters that he will give Saber a proper scolding when she wakes.
findings.explanation: A mock-threatening comic promise is reduced to merely mentioning the subject.

findings.highlight: Why are you looking at me if you’ve seen a ghost?
findings.evidenceJa: お化けでも見たような顔しちゃって
findings.governingReading: Rin asks why Shirou looks as though he has seen a ghost.
findings.explanation: The malformed conditional makes seeing a ghost the reason he should look at Rin.

findings.highlight: the Master will be informed of that
findings.evidenceJa: マスターにだって伝わる
findings.governingReading: A Servant beginning battle is conveyed to or felt by the Master through their bond.
findings.explanation: The passive “will be informed” suggests an external notification and blurs the magical link.

findings.highlight: English tea
findings.evidenceJa: 紅茶
findings.governingReading: Shirou distinguishes black tea from Japanese tea and notes that he only has teabags.
findings.explanation: The English substitutes a national category for the specific drink.

findings.highlight: her usual attitude
findings.evidenceJa: いつも通りの姿
findings.governingReading: Seeing Saber back in her familiar normal state brings Shirou’s complaints rushing back.
findings.explanation: Visible condition or appearance becomes behavioral attitude, implying conduct the source does not specify.

findings.highlight: We noticed the presence of a third Servant
findings.evidenceJa: 第三のサーヴァントに気が付き
findings.governingReading: Saber says that she noticed the third Servant observing their battle.
findings.explanation: The English assigns the detection to both combatants instead of Saber.

findings.highlight: if I’m going to let you fight, I’m going to fight myself
findings.evidenceJa: おまえに戦わせるぐらいなら、俺が自分で戦う
findings.governingReading: Rather than make Saber fight, Shirou says he will fight himself.
findings.explanation: The English conditional can mean that he will let her fight and join her, reversing the substitution at the center of his claim.

findings.highlight: My body is that of a heroic spirit
findings.evidenceJa: この身は既に英霊
findings.governingReading: Saber declares that she herself now exists as a Heroic Spirit.
findings.explanation: A formal self-reference is literalized as anatomy, narrowing her claim about status and identity to her body.

findings.highlight: I can’t allow someone to get hurt, In place of saving me.
findings.evidenceJa: 無力な自分を守って。その代わりに“誰か”が傷つくのは許せない
findings.governingReading: Shirou cannot accept someone being hurt in exchange for protecting his powerless self.
findings.explanation: Broken syntax obscures the exchange relation that connects his survivor psychology to his justice ideal.

findings.highlight: I might at least be able to sneak an attack on them
findings.evidenceJa: 寝首をかく事ぐらいできる
findings.governingReading: Shirou argues that preparation might let him catch a Servant completely unawares, literally at its sleeping throat.
findings.explanation: The English weakens a concrete lethal idiom into any surprise attack.

findings.highlight: A shield prepared by you
findings.evidenceJa: シロウの立てた守り
findings.governingReading: Saber dismisses whatever defenses or protective measures Shirou devises as paper-thin.
findings.explanation: The English invents a single physical shield and narrows the tactical claim.

findings.highlight: insulting the Servants
findings.evidenceJa: サーヴァントを侮っている
findings.governingReading: Saber accuses Shirou of underestimating Servants.
findings.explanation: A judgment about dangerous miscalculation becomes a social offense.

findings.highlight: It’s no use.
findings.evidenceJa: 話は平行線で、一向に交わる気配さえない
findings.governingReading: The narration says their positions remain parallel with no sign of meeting.
findings.explanation: The classic branch inserts an explicit verdict of futility absent from the active Japanese.

findings.highlight: It looks this conversation is going nowhere
findings.evidenceJa: 話は平行線で
findings.governingReading: The conversation appears to be going nowhere.
findings.explanation: The English omits the required “like” or “as though,” producing malformed prose.

findings.highlight: he just doesn’t want to get you hurt
findings.evidenceJa: 貴女が傷を負うのを嫌がってる
findings.governingReading: Rin says Shirou simply hates the prospect of Saber suffering injury.
findings.explanation: The causative phrasing can make Shirou the person who gets Saber hurt, blurring the object of his concern.

findings.highlight: That’s emotional flab on your mind
findings.evidenceJa: それは心の贅肉よ
findings.governingReading: Rin calls Saber’s proposal “fat on the heart,” repeating her earlier metaphor for needless sentiment.
findings.explanation: The English mixes emotional and mental glosses into a redundant, Japanese-shaped phrase that dulls the callback.

findings.highlight: The two talk dangerously.
findings.evidenceJa: なにやら物騒な物言いをするお二人さん
findings.governingReading: Shirou wryly remarks on the ominous way the two ladies are talking.
findings.explanation: The English is unnatural and drops the narrator’s lightly comic address to the pair.

findings.highlight: teach him about magic
findings.evidenceJa: 魔術講座
findings.governingReading: Rin claims the magecraft-instruction side of Shirou’s training.
findings.explanation: The English collapses the work’s technical term for magecraft into generic magic.

findings.highlight: I will have you train in the dojo tomorrow
findings.evidenceJa: 道場で汗を流してもらいます
findings.governingReading: Saber says Shirou will work up a sweat in the dojo tomorrow.
findings.explanation: The English preserves training but removes the physical idiom and its quietly threatening comic force.

findings.highlight: Everything starts from my body.
findings.evidenceJa: 何事も体が資本
findings.governingReading: For anything one undertakes, the body or health is the essential capital.
findings.explanation: A Japanese proverb is copied into an opaque English claim about bodily origin.

findings.highlight: if my body is well-prepared, I can overcome any hardships
findings.evidenceJa: どんな責め苦だろうと体さえしっかりしていれば乗り切れるといいな、なんて、儚い望み
findings.governingReading: Shirou clings to the frail hope that a sound body might carry him through whatever torment awaits.
findings.explanation: “Hardships” euphemizes torment, while the frailty of the hope and the act of clinging to it disappear.
